text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.6% today as oil prices dropped on easing Middle East tensions. Yesterday's news that U.S.-Iran peace efforts were reviving calmed markets' fears of supply disruptions, which had driven oil higher the day before. With crude falling from recent highs, the margin refiners earn—the spread between what they pay for oil and what they get selling gasoline and diesel—compressed, weighing on the stock.

The decline fits a two-week slide of nearly 11%, driven by the whipsaw between geopolitical alarm and diplomatic relief. Refinery utilization remains solid at 92.8%, but without the fear premium that had lifted oil prices earlier in the week, the refining business has become less profitable in the near term.
